h: Snowdrops, silver birches and a day near the fens
p: Winter is when Anglesey Abbey really shows off. The winter garden is famous for its displays of colourful stems, scented shrubs and carpets of snowdrops in February. The grove of white-barked Himalayan birches is the showstopper, glowing against grey winter skies, and it's a favourite with photographers.

Come back in summer and the mood changes completely. The borders burst into colour, the dahlia garden puts on a big show, and the long avenues and wide lawns are perfect for a gentle stroll or a picnic.

Inside the house, Lord Fairhaven's eye for collecting shows at every turn, from paintings and furniture to clocks and silver. It's a cosy, lived-in kind of country house rather than a vast palace, which makes it easy to explore at a relaxed pace.
Allow half a day to see the house, gardens and mill without rushing. The paths are mostly flat, which makes it good for pushchairs and wheelchairs, and there are places to eat on site.

Lode is just north-east of Cambridge, so it's easy to combine with a trip into the city for the colleges, the river and the museums. Wicken Fen, another National Trust site and one of the oldest nature reserves in the country, is a short drive north, perfect if you fancy a walk among the reeds and wildlife. Racing fans can carry on east to Newmarket, the home of British horse racing.
